question: Which of the following temples is built in the hoyasala architectural style?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesava Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Kesava Temple, also known as the Chennakesava Temple, is located in Somanathapura in the Indian state of Karnataka.

• It was constructed in the 13th century by the Hoysala Empire, which is known for its unique and intricate architectural style.

• The Hoysala architectural style is characterized by detailed sculptures, intricate carvings, and star-shaped platforms.

• The temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna and is a fine example of Hoysala architecture, showcasing the artistic and engineering skills of the period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Hoysala Architecture**

• The Hoysala Empire ruled most of what is now Karnataka between the 10th and 14th centuries.

• Their architectural style is unique to southern India and is most recognizable for its star-shaped platforms and intricate detailing.

• Hoysala temples often feature multiple shrines and are constructed using soapstone, which allows for detailed carvings.

• Famous Hoysala temples include the Chennakesava Temple at Belur and the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu.

• **Ladkhan Temple**

• The Ladkhan Temple is one of the oldest Hindu temples located in Aihole, Karnataka.

• It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is an example of early Chalukyan architecture.

• **Konark Temple**

• The Konark Sun Temple is located in Odisha and is a 13th-century temple dedicated to the Sun God.

• It is an example of Kalinga architecture and is famous for its intricate stone carvings.

• **Khajuraho Temple**

• The Khajuraho Group of Monuments is located in Madhya Pradesh and is known for its Nagara-style architectural symbolism and its erotic sculptures.

• These temples were built by the Chandela dynasty between 950 and 1050 AD.
